input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Publish platform structured logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention that all
RHOAI component adoptions build against: a JSON log-record schema, the set of
required fields, and per-language library guidance. It is the prerequisite
design work for every per-component adoption in this strategy.

## Scope

- Author the structured logging convention covering:
  - JSON schema for a log record
  - Required fields: timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id
  - Library guidance for Go, Python, and TypeScript
- Publish the convention where adopting teams can reference it
- Socialize the convention with the owning teams of the adopting components
  (Dashboard, serving, pipelines, model registry, TrustyAI, workbenches,
  distributed workloads) so adoptions can proceed mechanically

## Acceptance Criteria

- The convention document is published and defines a machine-validatable JSON
  schema for log records
- The schema requires the fields timestamp, level, component, namespace, and
  correlation id
- Library guidance is included for Go, Python, and TypeScript
- Review/acceptance of the convention is recorded from each adopting
  component's owning team

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id),
  and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript)

# Adopt structured logging convention in Dashboard

## Description

Convert the Dashboard's logging to the platform structured logging convention
so its log output is machine-queryable and correlates with other components'
logs via the shared required fields.

## Scope

- Update Dashboard logging to emit convention-conformant JSON records with the
  required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id)
- Ensure request handling emits the correlation id field so a user action can
  be traced across the platform
- Update any log-parsing or log-dependent tooling within the component to the
  new format

## Acceptance Criteria

- All log records emitted by the Dashboard validate against the published
  convention's JSON schema, including the required fields timestamp, level,
  component, namespace, and correlation id
- Existing Dashboard functionality is unchanged apart from log format (the
  component's test suite passes)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs
